title: U.S. Grand Jury Charges 'El R-1' and Brother 'El R-2' as CJNG's 'Los Rs' Cell Reorganizes Under New Leadership
detail: Infobae reported August 27, 2026 that a federal grand jury in the District of Columbia filed an indictment against Ramón Ángel Álvarez Ayala ('El R-1') — the 'Los Rs' cell leader arrested July 30, 2026 in Atotonilco el Alto, Jalisco, and linked to the November 1, 2025 assassination of former Uruapan mayor Carlos Manzo — and his brother Rafael Álvarez Ayala ('El R-2'), who Mexican authorities have identified as R-1's successor atop Los Rs, a CJNG-affiliated cell operating across Apatzingán, Uruapan, and Morelia in Michoacán and Jalisco. Both brothers face charges of conspiracy to distribute cocaine and methamphetamine for import into the United States, plus firearms offenses, carrying a mandatory minimum of 40 years and a maximum of two consecutive life sentences each; the underlying DEA-Los Angeles investigation spans 2004 through December 2023. Unlike R-1, R-2 remains at large and is now a named U.S. target, illustrating CJNG's franchise cells reconstituting leadership from within family/cell networks rather than fracturing after a capture.

title: Suspected CJNG Explosives Ambush Wounds 2 FRIZ Officers Near El Chique Dam, Zacatecas — First of a Three-Attack Wave
detail: On the morning of Thursday, August 27, 2026, Fuerza de Reacción Inmediata Zacatecas (FRIZ) officers patrolling toward Jalpa were ambushed with homemade dynamite devices roughly 30km short of their destination, near the El Chique dam in the San Luis community, Tabasco municipality, Zacatecas — about 115km southwest of Zacatecas City. Two FRIZ officers sustained minor injuries during at least two explosions and a sustained exchange of gunfire; related confrontations were reported the same day near the Los Soyates ranch (Villanueva municipality) and the Los Serna dam across the state line in Calvillo, Aguascalientes. Zacatecas State Prosecutor Cristian Paul Camacho Osnaya later said CJNG could be linked to this attack and to two further attacks in the following days (Aug 29 Villa García, Aug 30 Ojocaliente), making it the first of three suspected CJNG explosives attacks on Zacatecas police within a week.
